text:
Frederic Brunet came back from an injury on Nov. 5 in Pittsburgh, according to NHL.com's practice report, and he's been on the ice for a winning team ever since. The 23-year-old has 5 points in 12 games, two on the power play, in what amounts to his rookie season.

Our numbers are blunt about how. Boston has scored 8.7 more goals than its chances deserve with Brunet on the ice, and the Bruins take just 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him at five on five, eight points worse than without him. His own offense is light, 0.45 expected goals all season, and his shot is in the 7th percentile for speed.

So this is a young defenseman getting results that will even out. That isn't a knock: he was a 2022 fifth-round pick from Rimouski who scored 73 points in his last junior season and spent time in Providence. Sticking in an NHL lineup on a 13-4-1 team is the win. Our projection runs wide, 17 to 39 points, because the sample is short. The thing to watch is his shot share once the goals stop going in for his pair.
headline: Brunet's run of luck
